Lesson 13.1 · 24 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Problem framing, scope and stakeholders

After this lesson you can:
  • Write an outcome-based problem statement
  • Map decision owners and affected actors
  • Control assumptions and scope boundaries
On this page
  1. Start with the decision
  2. Stakeholder map
  3. Scope evidence
  4. Where this lives in LoanOS
  5. Knowledge check

1. Start with the decision

State the borrower or operating problem, measurable outcome, regulatory constraint and decision being improved.

Avoid beginning with a screen or requested feature.

Record current baseline, target and excluded outcomes.

2. Stakeholder map

Identify borrower, RE business owner, risk, credit, compliance, legal, operations, finance, technology, information security, partner and control approver. Use RACI only after decision rights and segregation constraints are understood.

3. Scope evidence

Maintain glossary, assumptions, policy sources, capability maturity and dependency map. Mark tenant configuration, external provider, UAT and production-admission work explicitly; implementation in the platform is not proof of operating readiness.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-IT-GRC — Requirements, change and test evidence must support controlled, auditable processing.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability REG-009 — Regulatory applicability.
  • Capability REG-010 — Obligation ownership.
  • Capability PLT-005 — Admission and readiness.

Key terms

RE Tenant Evidence pack

Knowledge check

1. What is the weakest starting requirement?

  1. Reduce application abandonment from verified baseline
  2. Add a new status screen
  3. Meet a cited KFS control
  4. Shorten an owned manual decision
Show answer

B. A requested screen assumes a solution without defining the problem, decision or outcome.
